{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows no positive signal (sentiment=0.00) and model overestimates prices.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude by 5-10% if recent history shows mean reversion toward lower prices (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days of declining prices).",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices if sentiment history includes a 0.50 or higher positive signal, indicating potential rebound.",
    "Apply lag correction: if true outcome is significantly lower than forecast, adjust next forecast downward by 10-15% to account for delayed market reaction.",
    "Cap forecast spikes above 10% above recent 15-day high — avoid over-optimism after sharp price increases.",
    "If true outcome is consistently higher than forecast over 3+ consecutive days, apply a downward bias correction to prevent overconfidence in model’s upward momentum.",
    "When sentiment history includes 0.25 or higher, increase forecast volatility to reflect market uncertainty or potential breakout.",
    "For 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast variance if historical error shows high overfitting to recent highs (e.g., >20% deviation from true outcome)."
  ]
}
